key_insight: A hybrid front-surface nanocone plus absorber nanohole architecture improves thin-film silicon solar-cell light trapping by reducing reflection and boosting internal optical confinement.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical path to higher-efficiency, thermally robust thin-film silicon photovoltaics without increasing absorber thickness.
method: Optimize nanocone and nanohole geometry with FDTD optical simulations
Couple optical results to electrical device modeling under optimized doping
Test performance with coupled opto-electro-thermal simulations from isothermal to 45°C
evidence_signal: The optimized device reaches 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% FF, and 24.42% PCE, with 95.21% efficiency retained at 45°C.
watch_item: Fabrication complexity and nanoscale alignment of the hybrid nanocone-nanohole structure may challenge large-area manufacturability.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
